subject: Request: custom uptime exhibit + order form language for Cardinal Health integration
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@cardinalhealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procure-admin@cardinalhealth.com>, Tara Singh <tara.singh@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Availability exhibit for Redwood integration

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about the latency and failover behavior you showed. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete ask so we can move the Cardinal Health integration forward.

High level ask: we need a tailored uptime exhibit (SLA addendum) that includes:
- 99.95% monthly availability for the dedicated integration endpoint used by Cardinal (single-tenant pool)
- A per-minute latency SLO for 95th percentile API calls (target <= 120ms for the critical inference path)
- Clear incident/credit calculation and a 72-hour target for initial incident communications

We anticipate signing an order form in the next 30 days pending this language. Procurement has attached the standard Cardinal order form template (we can share separately) — they will want the Redwood order form SKU lines and pricing to match.

Can you share a redline of your SLA addendum that maps to those items and any evidence (SOC2, uptime posture) we can attach to the procurement package? Also note we may ask for a limited availability exception for cross-region failover windows during major version rollouts.

Thanks,
Oliver

--
Oliver Grant
Director, Cloud Integrations
Cardinal Health Systems

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability exhibit for Redwood integration

Oliver —

Appreciate the clear asks. I attached an initial redline of a bespoke SLA addendum and a draft order form SKU sheet for your procurement team to review (files: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_Draft_v1.docx, OrderForm_SKUs_2027.xlsx).

Quick notes up front:
- We can support 99.95% monthly availability for a dedicated pool configuration with reserved capacity; we'll call that out as an addendum exhibit tied to the Order Form.
- Per-minute latency SLO: we generally publish token-level latency for shared models, but for dedicated endpoints we can commit to a 95th percentile request latency <= 120ms for the defined request envelope (payloads <= 2k tokens). We want to add a carve-out for long-running batched inference and larger payloads.
- Incident communication: 72-hour initial notification is fine; for severity 1 incidents we request a 4-hour on-call acknowledgement. Credits will be calculated on a monthly basis, capped per the Order Form.

Outstanding asks where we need clarity from your side:
1) Which endpoints are considered "critical inference paths" (API route names or internal product IDs)?
2) Expected peak qps and acceptable burst profile — this determines whether we recommend dedicated capacity vs. dedicated subnet (affects order form SKUs).
3) Are cross-region failover windows acceptable with a defined maintenance SLA (we propose a 4-hour planned failover window with a 48-hour notice for major upgrades)?

Looping in Laura (Legal) and Marcus (Solutions/Product) to align on redline items and evidence we can share (SOC2).

Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@cardinalhealth.com>, procure-admin@cardinalhealth.com
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Availability exhibit for Redwood integration

Thanks Camila —

Laura (Legal) here. I reviewed the redline and highlighted two contract-level items that Procurement will likely prioritize:
- Credit calculation formula: Cardinal's template expects daily credits; our standard is monthly aggregation with a cap. We should propose a compromise formula that shows a monthly calculation but with an explicit per-incident minimum credit threshold.
- Definition of "unavailable": we need a precise API-level definition (HTTP 5xx + upstream timeouts > threshold) and exclusions (maintenance, DDoS, third-party outages).

Marcus — can you confirm the technical carve-outs for batched/large payloads and whether a 120ms p95 is supported for the dedicated configuration they requested? If not, propose the quantization/instance types we recommend.

I'll draft a short procurement-friendly paragraph to add to the addendum explaining credit caps and exclusions.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Availability exhibit for Redwood integration

Laura / Camila —

Short technical note:
- 120ms p95: achievable on dedicated NVL GPUs with our low-latency kernel stack for inference if the payload is <= 2k tokens and KV cache warm starts are enabled. We can document the configuration in the addendum (instance types, reserved pool size, and routing policy).
- For batched jobs and sequences >2k tokens, latency will vary; propose we exclude those from the 120ms SLO and instead create a separate SLO class.
- Cross-region failover: we can support an RTO target for automatic regional failover, but warm cache transfer may introduce up to 30s additional latency during cutover. Recommend a plan where failover is coordinated (48h notice for planned) and automatic for P1 incidents.

I'll assemble a short technical exhibit to attach (configuration + recommended SKUs) and share a SOC2 extract that documents controls relevant to availability.

Marcus Lin
Principal Product Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@cardinalhealth.com>, procure-admin@cardinalhealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Availability exhibit for Redwood integration

Oliver / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clarity. Attached: updated SLA addendum redline (Redwood_SLA_Addendum_Draft_v1.docx), a recommended configuration exhibit, and order form SKU sheet (OrderForm_SKUs_2027.xlsx). We also included a SOC2 extract (SOC2_Report_Redwood_2026.pdf) that calls out availability controls.

Highlights of the attached redline:
- Availability: 99.95% monthly for the dedicated integration endpoint; exceptions and calculation algorithm are spelled out in Section 2.1.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 120ms when requests meet the payload/instance criteria; section 2.2 lists exclusions (batched inference, >2k tokens, scheduled maintenance).
- Incident handling: initial S1 acknowledgement within 4 hours; full monthly credit calculation with per-incident floor.
- Cross-region failover: documented operational plan and a 30s warm-cache cutover note; proposed 48-hour notice for planned major rollouts.

Next steps we propose:
1) Procurement review the redline and mark required commercial items. If you need daily-level credits instead of monthly aggregation, let us know and Laura will propose a bridging formula.
2) Confirm critical endpoints and projected peak qps; Aditya (copied) can run a quick capacity sketch and map SKUs.
3) If the addendum language looks good, we can push to DocuSign next week and align the order form lines to the Cardinal template.

Aditya — can you prepare a short capacity note (1 page) that maps Cardinal's projected qps to recommended reserved pool sizes and expected monthly cost delta?

Appreciate the collaboration — happy to do a 30-min call to walk through the redline if that helps.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_Draft_v1.docx (37KB), OrderForm_SKUs_2027.xlsx (14KB), SOC2_Report_Redwood_2026.pdf (220KB)
